messages:
maria_cs: Customer: CSV download is arriving as a 0-byte file (no headers). Happens when they select 'Last 90 days' + segment filter. Two customers reported it. Screenshot: https://redwood.s3.amazonaws.com/exports/zero-byte.png

josh_support: Thanks — can you paste the export job id and what browser they used? Did they try downloading from incognito or curl? Any console/network errors?

maria_cs: Job ID from UI: exp-9876. Customer used Chrome 111 on Win10. They tried opening in Excel and also saving via right-click -> Save link as, both gave 0 bytes. Said it started after yesterday's deploy. No console errors on client.

josh_support: Reproducing locally now with same filters. If I request the download URL and do `curl -I` I see headers that look wrong:

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/csv
Content-Encoding: gzip
Content-Length: 0
Accept-Ranges: bytes
ETag: "abc123"
```

josh_support: attaching a tiny server log snippet from the worker that ran the job: 

```
2026-02-02T12:34:21Z INFO ExportJob exp-9876 - generating /tmp/export-9876.csv rows=234567
2026-02-02T12:34:52Z INFO Uploader S3 - starting multipart upload export-9876.csv.gz
2026-02-02T12:34:53Z INFO Uploader S3 - upload complete bytes=0 key=exports/exp-9876.csv.gz
2026-02-02T12:34:53Z ERROR ExportJob exp-9876 - finished with 0 bytes
```

josh_support: I can repro 100% locally when export > ~200k rows. Smaller exports succeed.

liam_eng: @josh_support thanks for the trace. My initial guess: streaming gzip path is setting Content-Length=0 (we used to stream without content-length for chunked uploads). S3 sometimes accepts the parts but the way our uploader wrapper handles the gzip stream leads to an empty final object when the upstream sets an explicit content-length header of 0. Probably a bug introduced in upload-service v1.4.7 (recent deploy).

liam_eng: Quick repro commands I used:

```
# request presigned url and then stream upload
curl -X PUT -T <(gzip -c big.csv) "https://presigned.s3.url/..." -v
# response shows 200 but curl reports 0 length when we later HEAD
curl -I "https://cdn.redwood.ai/exports/exp-9876.csv.gz"
```

sophia_analytics: Noted that the failure correlates with date ranges that produce >200k rows (longer timeframes). Might be a memory/streaming threshold.

liam_eng: Root cause hypothesis: we added an on-the-fly gzip streaming optimization to reduce disk IO. In certain code paths the worker closes the gzip stream before flushing underlying buffer, then the uploader initiates a multipart S3 upload using that stream object. Because our wrapper reads Content-Length from the stream (and it returns 0 for the closed buffer), we end up writing a zero-length object.

liam_eng: Immediate mitigation: revert the streaming gzip change in upload-service (roll back 1.4.7 -> 1.4.6) and re-run affected exports. I'll open a PR with a proper fix to fully write+flush the temp gzip file before upload, or else avoid setting Content-Length when streaming.

deploy-bot: @liam_eng triggered rollback for `upload-service` from 1.4.7 -> 1.4.6. Rollback job: rb-2026-02-02-14:12 (in progress) :arrow_down:

sre_oncall: Created incident INC-2026-224: export-service zero-byte uploads. Raising alert to 15m. Monitoring export success rate and S3 putObject errors.

josh_support: Workaround for affected customers: ask them to (a) narrow date range to <30 days, or (b) use JSON export (works), or (c) request support to re-run the job after we've rolled back. I've messaged the two impacted accounts with the temporary workaround and offered to re-run exports.

liam_eng: Fix plan: (1) revert streaming gzip in hotfix (done by deploy-bot), (2) add unit/integration test covering large export streams + multipart upload, (3) change uploader to not set Content-Length when reading from non-seekable streams, (4) release 1.4.8 with tests. Assign RNWD-4321 to eng-runtime.

josh_support: Thanks. I'll mark the tickets and update customers after the rollback completes.

maria_cs: @sophia_analytics can you add dashboard checks to detect empty export downloads (Content-Length=0) and spike alerts so we catch regressions faster?

sophia_analytics: Yep — I'll add a metric for export_success_rate by bundle-size and a separate alert for content-length=0 responses.

liam_eng: After rollback, I re-ran exp-9876 and confirmed a good file uploaded (gzipped size 18MB, Content-Length header present). Closing urgent loop; leaving RNWD-4321 open for the proper fix and tests.

josh_support: Closing thread when incident resolved but keeping RNWD-4321 referenced in the customer tickets.

maria_cs: Thanks everyone. Re-run scheduled for impacted customers and customers notified. :white_check_mark:
